The magnitude_feedback block separates those error kinds deterministically: classify each miss first as a direction error (missed_surge or binary false positive) or a class error (underestimate or overestimate), then attribute causes. Do not reward confidence merely for increasing. Record known error facts separately from causal hypotheses. A correct prediction does not prove that its reasons caused the outcome or were sufficient. Return only an object with reflection_items (array) and selected_reflection_refs (array of supplied lower-level item refs), and no_findings_reason (null or a specific reason when both arrays are empty). Each authored item has exactly: category, kind (fact/hypothesis/action), brief, detail, scope ({case_refs:[], plan_refs:[], conditions:string}), limitations (string array), source_refs (nonempty supplied-reference array), counter_refs (supplied-reference array), and outcome_claims (array of {source_ref, axis:binary|magnitude, correct:boolean}). Allowed categories are ['decision_drivers', 'why_prediction_failed', 'misleading_signals', 'ignored_evidence', 'missing_information', 'plan_issues']. Runtime supplies IDs, level and evidence status; never author them. One item makes one main observation, explanation or action. Generate complete detail and a self-contained actionable brief together: retain the triggering condition, concrete finding/action and material caveat; a title or 'improve research' is insufficient. The brief must not add claims or turn an uncertain explanation into an established rule. Cite exact supplied source handles. All scope case_refs/plan_refs must be supported by those sources. Every outcome claim's source_ref must also appear in that same item's source_refs: list each claim-cited item in source_refs exactly once. State contrary cases in counter_refs and limitations. Success/failure assertions require outcome_claims matching the canonical source facts; technical exclusions cannot be research successes or failures. Category and claim correctness are linked: successful_patterns and decision_drivers items may carry only correct=true claims, while failed_patterns, why_prediction_failed, false_positive_patterns, and false_negative_patterns items may carry only correct=false claims. A mixed outcome is not a fact error: when binary direction was right but magnitude was wrong (or the reverse), author separate items — the correct axis as one success-category item, the incorrect axis as one failure-category item — instead of one item whose claims straddle both. Author at most 6 new items in one response and prefer selecting existing lower-level items by ref; a complete response with fewer items beats a truncated one. A realized return does not establish why it occurred: label causal explanations as hypotheses and propose a test. Source references establish provenance, not correctness. Higher levels act as a sieve: select useful existing items by ref without rewriting them; author only new sourced comparisons or actions. Repeated versions of one case do not constitute independent evidence. Empty arrays are valid when there is no supported additional lesson; do not invent findings to fill categories. Each operation has op and path; replace/add/append also have value. Use only issued permissions.
